title: Knowledge check: Reactivity Debugging and Best Practices

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Reactivity Debugging and Best Practices”?
options: Destructuring always preserves reactive tracking automatically.
Use computed() for pure derived values and watchers for side effects caused by reactive changes.
A computed getter should send network requests every time it is evaluated.
Refs in script do not use .value.
questions.answer_key: Use computed() for pure derived values and watchers for side effects caused by reactive changes.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Reactivity Debugging and Best Practices directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Destructuring reactive objects safely”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use reactive() for an object whose nested properties are tracked, and avoid destructuring in ways that lose the property connection.
reactive() turns every primitive into a ref automatically.
Destructuring always preserves a reactive link to each primitive property.
A reactive object must be copied into local state before every update.
questions.answer_key: Use reactive() for an object whose nested properties are tracked, and avoid destructuring in ways that lose the property connection.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Destructuring reactive objects safely”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Reactivity Debugging and Best Practices” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
